A LOOK AHEAD

One question.
Many possible futures.

AFTERMATH explores when the tasks in a job could be fully automated. Some need better AI. Others also need advances in robotics, sensing, and safety.

Choose a job, explore three possible timelines, and see what would need to happen. You can edit the tasks to match your work.

These are possibilities, not predictions.

The year uses dated milestone evidence and explicit transfer assumptions. Measured software progress and expert forecasts are distinguished. Missing evidence stays visible; a generic future date is never substituted. These are conditional scenarios, not validated whole-job predictions.

Occupational data: O*NET, European Commission ESCO, and ILO ISCO. Source categories overlap and do not enumerate every possible future job.

Data credits & coverage +

O*NET 31.0 Database, U.S. Department of Labor/Employment and Training Administration, used under CC BY 4.0. AFTERMATH restructures the data and adds its own model. USDOL/ETA has not approved, endorsed, or tested these modifications. O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA.

This service uses the ESCO classification of the European Commission. ESCO classification © European Union, reused with attribution under the European Commission reuse policy. English occupation concepts and skill relationships are preserved. Task-level robot assessments and cited references come from Legate-Yang and Massenkoff / Anthropic under CC BY 4.0, using O*NET 29.3. These are published AI-assisted assessments, not independent trials. ISCO factual unit-group codes and titles are included with ILO source links; older copyrighted duty definitions are not republished.

Source editions, download hashes, transformation scripts, model research, and the ongoing project log are in the public repository.

Privacy & project details +

Your search and report stay in this browser. No account, saved searches, or AI API calls. GitHub hosts the site; Google Fonts serves the typeface. Downloads stay on your device.
